claim: Lou, Polk and Skouras (JFE 2019): the value-weight decile long/short on past-month overnight returns earns a three-factor overnight alpha of 3.47% per month (t 16.83) and an intraday alpha of -3.02% per month (t -9.74); the premia of the strategies studied are earned overnight, with opposite-signed intraday legs.
limitations: Uses first-print or official open depending on the data set; no transaction costs; the text states t 16.83 for the three-factor alpha while hypotheses.md cites t 16.6 (raw Table 1 figure); the difference is not material to the frozen gates.
independent_replication: Akbas et al. 2022 and Lachance 2023 report related persistence; no independent tradability study with costs.
impact_on_spec: Sets the 16 bp/night gross magnitude that the decision cell must reach; supplies the tug-of-war signal used for TOW_21.

claim: Aboody, Even-Tov, Lehavy and Trueman (JFQA 2018): stocks in the top overnight-return decile in week w have a significantly higher average overnight return in week w+1 than the lowest decile; the difference is 1.76 percentage points, decreasing but still reliably positive for weeks w+2 to w+4.
quote: The difference in the average overnight return for week w + 1 is an economically large 1.76 percentage points.
limitations: Equal-weight, includes small and illiquid stocks; no costs; published date is the journal year, month approximate.
independent_replication: Lou-Polk-Skouras 2019 report persistence with different sorting horizon and weighting.
impact_on_spec: Sets the ON_5 (one-week) candidate and the second decision cell ON5_P1500_LS.

claim: Akbas, Boehmer, Jiang and Koch (JFE 2022): a higher frequency of positive overnight returns followed by negative trading day reversals during a month indicates a more intense daily tug of war between noise traders overnight and arbitrageurs during the day, and predicts higher future returns in the cross section.
quote: a more intense daily tug of war predicts higher future returns in the cross section
limitations: Original page blocked by an anti-bot page (Incapsula, 200 with empty body); text read through https://r.jina.ai/ mirror of the same URL. Close-to-close future returns, not overnight-only.
independent_replication: Related to Lou-Polk-Skouras 2019; no independent replication opened.
impact_on_spec: Explains why holding the whole day nets to about zero (the repo's close-to-close cards) and motivates the overnight-only leg.

claim: Bogousslavsky (JFE 2021): margin requirements are higher overnight and lending fees are typically charged only on positions held overnight, which pushes arbitrageurs to reduce positions before the close; a mispricing factor earns positive returns throughout the day but performs poorly at the end of the day, more so in the second half of the sample.
quote: lending fees are typically charged only on positions held overnight
limitations: Abstract only (EconPapers page); full text is paywalled.
independent_replication: Consistent with Lou-Polk-Skouras 2019 and Akbas et al. 2022.
impact_on_spec: Justifies charging borrow for the overnight short leg and treating the last-hour and overnight legs as differently priced.

claim: Heston, Korajczyk and Sadka (JF 2010): there is a striking pattern of return continuation at half-hour intervals that are exact multiples of a trading day, lasting at least 40 trading days; short-term reversal is driven by temporary liquidity imbalances lasting less than an hour.
quote: a striking pattern of return continuation at half-hour intervals that are exact multiples of a trading day
limitations: Abstract page read; the paper is about half-hour periodicity, used here only as a contrast.
independent_replication: Haendler et al. 2025 report out-of-sample persistence.
impact_on_spec: Contrast source for the open/close periodicity (queued as T-20260930-13); not a candidate here.

claim: Haendler, Heston, Korajczyk and Sadka (SSRN 5749704, 2025): the intra-day periodicity patterns persist out-of-sample; proxies for institutional trading (lendable shares, VWAP-like trading, index inclusion) explain the open and midday periodicity, and the results suggest open periodicity is driven by VWAP trading while close periodicity is driven by market-on-close trading.
quote: the results suggest that open periodicity is driven by VWAP trading while close periodicity by market-on-close trading
limitations: Abstract page only; working paper, not peer reviewed.
independent_replication: Replicates Heston et al. 2010 out of sample by the same authors.
impact_on_spec: Recent evidence that flow-driven open/close patterns persist; background for the auction-execution framing.

claim: Goyal, Jegadeesh and Wu (JFQA 2026, NYSE and Nasdaq 2012-2021): closing auctions carry about 10% of daily volume and have lower price impact than the continuous market for all stocks except Nasdaq microcaps; opening auctions are illiquid and carry the largest price impact; anomaly long/short portfolios cost 17-41 bp per year.
quote: Closing auctions account for about 10% of daily trading volume
limitations: Costs annualized for low-turnover anomalies, not a nightly book; institutional-size orders.
independent_replication: SSRN 4300417 working paper; no independent replication found.
impact_on_spec: Supports the 2 bp per side auction cost contract and its 2x stress; warns that the opening leg is the expensive one.

claim: Alpaca orders: the cls time in force submits market-on-close and limit-on-close orders that execute only in the closing auction; cls orders submitted after 3:50pm ET and before 7:00pm ET are rejected; opg orders execute only in the opening auction and are rejected after 9:28am ET.
quote: This order is eligible to execute only in the market closing auction.
limitations: Documents order acceptance, not fill quality; paper cls fills untested, paper opg fills unreliable (45 of 50 expired on 2026-09-15).
impact_on_spec: Fixes the executable route: cls before 15:50 ET in, DAY market or opg before 09:28 ET out.

claim: Alpaca margin and short selling: $0 locate and borrow fees on all easy-to-borrow (ETB) shares for Trading API users; hard-to-borrow shares are charged.
quote: $0 locate and borrow fees on all ETB shares for Trading API users
limitations: Rendered web page without a versioned date; the design charges T-32 tiered borrow anyway as the conservative reading.
impact_on_spec: Shows the T-32 borrow tiers are conservative for ETB names; the ETB proxy (DTC quantile) is diagnostic (e).

claim: Salotra et al. (Risks 2026): overnight versus daytime static and momentum strategies on ten sector ETFs over 1999-2025 show that reversal strategies outperform buy-and-hold, but the outperformance decreases significantly with transaction costs of 1 bp versus 2 bp.
quote: This outperformance decreases significantly when transaction costs are taken into account.
limitations: Original page returned 403 to curl; text read through the https://r.jina.ai/ mirror. ETFs only, background for cost sensitivity.
independent_replication: Consistent with the LPS decomposition; no stock-level evidence.
impact_on_spec: Background for the 1-2 bp cost sensitivity used in the auction contract.

claim: Lachance (Review of Financial Economics 2023, 1995-2021): the past year's overnight return is the most important predictor of future overnight returns, followed by volatility, momentum and turnover; an overnight momentum strategy of picking the top decile of past-year overnight returns yields 37.5% annually versus -18.99% for the bottom decile.
quote: the past year's overnight return is the most important predictor of future overnight returns
limitations: Original page returned 403 to curl; text read through the https://r.jina.ai/ mirror (full text obtained, not only the snippet). Raw overnight returns, no execution costs.
